text:
alex_reynolds: Hey infra team — running into a hard stop creating a new GPU nodepool in us-east1. Cloud errors show we hit ENI/secondary-ip limits when provisioning A100s. Need guidance + quota request text. Project: redwood-inference-prod, region: us-east1, desired: 12 x a2-highgpu-1g (1 A100) nodepool initially, want room to grow to 48 nodes. Any immediate workarounds?

maya_ops: Yep seen this before. TL;DR options: 1) raise ENI and subnet secondary IP quotas (fast but needs cloud support), 2) enable trunking (AWS) / increase alias IP ranges (GCP) so more pods/node without blowing subnet, or 3) reduce pod-per-node expectation by running fewer pods per GPU (but impacts density).

sre-nick: +1 to trunking/alias ranges. Also consider packing pods per GPU using MIG or nvidia-device-plugin + kube-scheduler constraints so you can run multiple smaller pods per GPU instead of 1:1. That reduces total node count — might lower quota needs.

alex_reynolds: For context: our current max-pods default is 110 on the node image we use. But the cloud provider refuses new ENIs because the per-AZ ENI quota is exhausted. I don't want to handwave numbers to support — can someone draft the exact quotas to request? Also cost note: if we request many more ENIs we may end up with a bunch of unused IPs — want to optimize.

maya_ops: Draft below — we should open a cloud support case with these asks. I'll paste two versions (minimal + recommended). Use the minimal for immediate capacity, recommended for mid-term.

--- BEGIN SUPPORT TICKET (minimal) ---
Project/Account: redwood-inference-prod
Region: us-east1 / us-east1-b,c,d (multi-AZ)
Request: Increase network interface and secondary IP address quotas to allow provisioning of a2-highgpu-1g nodepool.
Current need: Provision 12 GPU nodes immediately (a2-highgpu-1g). Estimated required quotas:
- ENI quota (per-region): increase by 48 (to allow ~4 ENIs per node for CNI/runtime)
- Secondary IP addresses (per-subnet): increase by 600 (to accommodate pod density across 12 nodes)
Justification: We are deploying GPU workloads that create multiple pods per node; current subnet IP exhaustion prevents node creation.
Contact: maya_ops@redwood.com, alex_reynolds@redwood.com
--- END SUPPORT TICKET (minimal) ---

--- BEGIN SUPPORT TICKET (recommended mid-term) ---
Project/Account: redwood-inference-prod
Region: us-east1 (multi-AZ)
Request: Increase the following quotas to support planned GPU cluster growth and higher pod density:
- ENI quota (regional/AZ): increase to 400 (current X) to support up to 48 GPU nodes with ENI trunking fallbacks
- Assignable secondary IPs (per-VPC/subnet): increase to 5000 to avoid fragmentation during rolling updates
- Regional GPU quota (A100/A2 family): increase to 50 GPUs (we currently plan up to 48 nodes)
- External IP (ephemeral) quota: +100 (we use external egress for some debug tools)
Justification: Needed to provision and autoscale dedicated GPU pools for inference serving. We will implement alias IP ranges / trunking plus warm-pool strategies to avoid long term unused IP wastage.
Contact: infra@redwood.com
--- END SUPPORT TICKET (recommended) ---

cloud-support: Thanks — creating ticket now. Ticket ID: CSP-2026-4891. Estimated response 24-48h. Note: provider asked for current quota numbers; please provide outputs below and we'll attach.

sre-nick: Commands to run (paste outputs into ticket):
- AWS: aws ec2 describe-account-attributes --attribute-names max-instances-per-region (and) aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=instance-type,Values=a2*"
- GCP: gcloud compute regions describe us-east1 --project redwood-inference-prod
Also: kubectl get nodes -o wide && kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | grep -i pods

maya_ops: Also include the CNI configuration snapshot; for AWS CNI we should show WARM_ENI_TARGET and WARM_IP_TARGET; for GCP we should show ip-allocation for the node pool:
```
# example gcloud node-pool show snippet
--node-pool-name=gpu-pool
--node-config: --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g
--ip-allocation-policy:
  cluster-secondary-range-name: cluster-pods
  services-secondary-range-name: cluster-svc
```

alex_reynolds: Quick question: is increasing ENI quota to 400 realistic? That seems huge. What's the conservative bump to request so cloud support approves faster?

sre-nick: For immediate approval ask for conservative numbers: ENI +100, secondary IPs +1000. For the longer run the recommended numbers make sense. Also put a note that we'll follow up with VPC cleanup automation to release unused IPs. Cloud teams like a remediation plan.

maya_ops: I'll add a remediation paragraph to the ticket: we'll deploy warm-pool autoscaler that reclaims unused nodes after 30m, enable CNI trunking (where supported), and run a monthly IP address audit.

alex_reynolds: Perfect. @cloud-support please confirm when ticket transitions to 'escalated' and paste the support link. If we get approval fast, we'll try create the 12-node pool tonight.

cloud-support: Ticket CSP-2026-4891 status: escalated -> ENG quota team. Link: https://cloudsupport.example.com/CSP-2026-4891. Will update within 36h.

deploy-bot: plan: gpu-pool-12 create started by alex_reynolds — currently blocked (quota).

alex_reynolds: Thanks all. If quota takes >48h plan B is to: a) temporarily create smaller non-GPU nodes for control-plane workloads, b) pack more pods per GPU using MIG + multi-container pods to minimize node count. We'll reconvene after ticket updates. :thumbsup:
